title: Count Positions on Street With Required Brightness
summary: Given an integer n , a street represented by a number line from 0 to n-1 , and a 2D integer array lights indicating the positions and ranges of street lamps, calculate the number of positions on the street that have a brightness of at least the specified requirement.
statement: Given an integer n , a street represented by a number line from 0 to n-1 , and a 2D integer array lights indicating the positions and ranges of street lamps, calculate the number of positions on the street that have a brightness of at least the specified requirement. Each street lamp lights up a segment of the street based on its position and range. The brightness at a position is defined as the number of street lamps that light up that position. An array requirement is provided, where each element specifies the minimum brightness required for the corresponding position on the street. The task is to count how many positions meet or exceed their respective brightness requirements.
constraints: Street positions are the integers zero through n-1.
A light [position,radius] illuminates the inclusive clipped interval position-radius through position+radius.
Brightness is the number of covering lights; count positions meeting or exceeding their individual requirement.
hints: Range additions can encode every lamp interval with two endpoint changes.
Add one at the clipped left endpoint and subtract one just after the clipped right endpoint.
Prefix-sum the change array and compare each brightness with its requirement.
Each lamp contributes one exactly throughout its interval; prefix accumulation combines all lamps, so each comparison uses the true brightness.
editorial: Each lamp contributes one exactly throughout its interval; prefix accumulation combines all lamps, so each comparison uses the true brightness.

tests.explanation: The computed brightness meets the requirement at four of the five positions.
With no lights, only the two positions requiring zero brightness qualify.
